name: 10 concurrent waiters, 1 matching mail -> exactly one gets the code
fix: Atomic consume must be the only delivery path

name: 10 waiters, 10 mails -> 10 distinct codes, none duplicated
20 waiters + 50 thread-notified scans, 1 mail -> 1 delivery, 1 consumed row
Store.consume(uv,uid) from 32 threads -> exactly one True
consume keys on (uidvalidity,uid): rollover re-delivers uid 7 once
mail that arrived BEFORE register is found immediately (register-then-search)
wait(after=now) must NOT return a 4-minute-old OTP (client just requested a fresh one)
fix: The 5-min CLOCK_SKEW_MARGIN is applied to BOTH the IMAP fetch and _matches, so any unconsumed OTP from the last 5 min is returned instantly -> job agent submits a stale/expired code. Gmail INTERNALDATE is server-assigned (no client skew), so use margin<=10-15s; or let callers pass `after` = their own request time and drop the margin; or track last-delivered per sender

name: two valid mails -> NEWEST delivered
conflict is returned once; later waiter still gets the next good mail
fix: Conflict message is not consumed, so it is re-evaluated (and re-409s) for every future waiter in the window while newer-first ordering saves only the case where a newer good mail exists; consume or blacklist a conflicting message after first report

name: reloaded orphan waiter is evaluated, result persisted, identical retry receives it
expired orphan waiter disappears from active_waiter_count on its own
fix: Prune expired orphans in active_waiter_count (filter by expires_at) and/or run a periodic sweeper task

name: waiter with after=0001-01-02 does not starve other waiters while pending
fix: scan() uses min(after) across ALL pending waiters; one OverflowError/odd date makes fetch_since raise for everyone (swallowed as 'scan failed'). Validate `after` on input (clamp to [now-1h, now+5m]) and evaluate waiters with independent fetch windows

name: timeout_s=2 honoured even if IMAP fetch hangs 6s
fix: Broker.wait awaits scan() OUTSIDE asyncio.wait_for. Wrap the whole register+scan+wait body in asyncio.timeout(timeout_s), and run initial scan as a task so the deadline can fire; also hold _scan_lock only around state changes, not IMAP I/O

name: short-timeout waiter is not stuck behind another waiter's slow scan
fetch_since raising -> waiter times out cleanly
fix: A broken mailbox is reported as 'timeout' (408) which a client cannot tell from 'no mail': return 503 {error: mailbox_unavailable} when scans fail for the entire wait

name: FastAPI-level: 2 concurrent POSTs, 1 mail -> one 200 (code) + one 408
timeout_s=99999 clamps server-side to <=300s
restart with short waiter (40s): client gets a clean, bounded outcome

fix: On shutdown resolve in-flight waiters with 503 {error:'restarting'} so clients get an explicit retryable error instead of a reset

name: restart with short waiter (40s): `systemctl restart` completes promptly (<15s)
observed: restart blocked 38.4s; new process answered 0.5s later
fix: uvicorn drains in-flight /v1/wait on SIGTERM, so every deploy/restart blocks until the longest waiter finishes or systemd SIGKILLs at 90s. Add --timeout-graceful-shutdown 5 and cancel waiters in lifespan shutdown

name: waiter recovered from SQLite after restart (short waiter (40s))
observed: active_waiter_count before=1 right after=0 (waiter finished during graceful drain; nothing to recover)
fix: Orphan reload only works if the old process is killed; clients must retry with identical parameters to pick up a stored result
